claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled 'SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi' exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ and covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration to Pulumi.
SST was originally built on AWS CDK, which allowed developers to define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.
AWS CDK is AWS-only and supports only TypeScript and Python, whereas Pulumi supports any programming language.
Ion is the code name for SST's new deployment engine, and once stable it will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
Pulumi lets you define infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C# and deploy to AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and on-premises.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account or Pulumi Cloud dependency; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps its state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account, not Pulumi Cloud.
Nitric runs application deployments through the Pulumi engine.
Defang runs application deployments through the Pulumi engine via a Pulumi provider.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, for deploying to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST apps define infrastructure and code together in a single `sst.config.ts` file.
Through 2023, SST's provisioning layer was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation.
In late 2023 the SST team began a rewrite code-named Ion that replaced the entire deployment layer.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'When you run `sst deploy`, those resources make a call to an embedded Pulumi engine that makes a call to their bridged Terraform provider, and this makes the AWS SDK calls to create your resources.'
SST docs 'What is SST' say: 'SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi.'
Gautier Blandin's article says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST's constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's article says: 'You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now.'
SST's platform package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds, and others, and a Pulumiverse Vercel provider.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, a network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools.
Nitric's docs state 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`.
AWS exposes hundreds of resource types.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed within the same SST app.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The `sst` npm package gets roughly 796,000 downloads per week (796,291 for September 5-11, 2026).
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode has a larger GitHub following than SST.
SST doesn't invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The SST repository is anomalyco/sst, formerly sst/sst.
